fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. Job says the opposite: "I will never say that you are right; I will maintain my integrity until I die." (Job 27:5) He isn't giving in to them, and he says so plainly. So that's a False, and a firm one.

That's it. Job says, "As long as I live, my conscience will not accuse me." (Job 27:6) He's saying his own inner voice has nothing to charge him with. That's a big claim, and I think he means every word.
Good guess, but the text doesn't say that. He says, "As long as I live, my conscience will not accuse me." (Job 27:6) The word is conscience, that inner voice. Pride never gets named in this verse.
Not the one Job asks. His question is about God: "Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him?" (Job 27:9) Friends don't come up in that verse. The question is about whether God hears.

That's right. Job asks, "Will he delight in the Almighty? Will he call upon God at all times?" (Job 27:10) Same man, same string of questions, one after another. Job keeps asking about the godless man in these verses.

Not this time, friend. Job says, "Though his sons are many, they are destined for the sword; and his offspring will never have enough food." (Job 27:14) Destined for the sword, with not enough food. So this one is False.

Right. Job says, "Though his sons are many, they are destined for the sword; and his offspring will never have enough food." (Job 27:14) Lots of sons, but destined for the sword. A heavy verse, so I'll just let it sit.
That's it. Job says, "…and their widows will not weep for them." (Job 27:15) It's a heavy line, and I think it's meant to sound that heavy. I'll just let it sit.
Not quite, friend. Job says the opposite: "…and their widows will not weep for them." (Job 27:15) Mourning for many days isn't what the verse says. It's a hard verse.
Not this one, friend. Job says, "…like a hut set up by a watchman." (Job 27:18) No prophets in that verse. It's a watchman's hut, a simple thing.

Not quite, friend. The verse says, "He lies down wealthy, but will do so no more…" (Job 27:19) Worry isn't mentioned. The point is that he's wealthy when he lies down, and when he opens his eyes, all is gone.
